$comment: The declared character set of each subset font, in pyftsubset --unicodes syntax.
Single-sourced because two things read it and they must not drift:
tools/build-fonts.sh        — builds the .woff2 files from it
tests/checks/18-font-coverage.test.js — asserts the site renders nothing outside it
A declared set that is narrower than the rendered text is not a build error. The
browser silently falls back to a synthesised face, mid-paragraph, and the page still
looks approximately right — which is the failure mode this repo exists to make
impossible to ship quietly. Check 18 turns it into a red build.
STATED LIMIT: check 18 proves the DECLARED set covers the copy. It does not decode
the woff2 to prove the shipped binary contains those glyphs. Closing that gap means
a woff2 decoder in Node, for a failure that requires someone to edit this file
without re-running tools/build-fonts.sh.
Archivo, Source Serif roman, IBM Plex Mono. Derived from the rendered text of every
page plus scorecard.md and the generated content in styles.css; FONTS.md carries the
per-codepoint inventory. Full printable ASCII is deliberate headroom — the pages use
86 of the 95, and carrying the other 9 means an editor can type '!' without a font
rebuild. U+201B is absent: no upstream family here has the glyph.
Source Serif 4 italic, and the only subset narrower than `shared`.
Italic resolves to a real face in exactly one place on this site: the eight .buyerq
pull-quotes on the rubric page. The inline <em> runs elsewhere compute to Archivo and
are synthesised obliques — they never fetch this file. Measured across all nine pages,
the characters actually rendered in Source Serif italic are 31: space, comma, question
mark, em dash, the four capitals D I T W, and every lowercase letter except j, x, z.
Declared here as 34 rather than those 31, and the difference is the whole judgement:
31 codepoints (exactly what renders)   9,776 B
34 (+ j, x, z — lowercase completed)  10,844 B   +1,068 B
68 (+ punctuation)                    16,352 B   +6,576 B
Completing lowercase costs 1,068 B for three glyphs and removes the likeliest edit
that would otherwise fall back: a new lowercase English word in a pull-quote.
Completing uppercase costs four times as much for letters that can only appear at the
start of a sentence. The asymmetry is measured, and the rule follows it rather than
the other way round. Everything past 34 is left to check 18, which turns a missing
glyph into a red build at the moment the copy changes — cheaper than carrying 6 KB
against the possibility.
This set was full printable ASCII (110 codepoints, 23,428 B) until 2026-08-09. The
13.6 KB that removed is what took /oal/ and /oal/v1.0/ from 151.5 KiB — over §4's
budget — to 139.2 KiB. It had to land before /oal/v1.0 first published, because
_headers caches that directory immutable and §5 freezes its contents: after the first
production deploy the font could never have been changed, and the overage would have
been permanent.
